finding: The v3.1 review evidently ran the suite with L12_TEST_TMP under ~/Documents: its review-tmp/ holds tmp312/ and tmp39/, and tmp39/ still holds a kit root (l12v3-5rksgne3, the kit's mkdtemp prefix); its suite copy was also under ~/Documents (review-tmp/run). On this Mac ~/Documents (and ~/Desktop, ~/Library/Mobile Documents) carries com.apple.file-provider-domain-id: iCloud Drive 'Desktop & Documents'. The provider changes the ctime of every newly written file there shortly after the write (100 of 100 files here; about 0.4 s and about 3 s after creation in two separate ad-hoc timing probes); a strict read that straddles that instant is INPUT_FILE_CHANGED (ctime_ns only). Under /private/tmp and $TMPDIR: 0 of 100 files changed, 0 refusals. The host (Linux, no File Provider) is not affected; the strict check stays.
fix: kit.safe_temp_parent skips any File Provider domain (kit.file_provider_domain); INPUT_FILE_CHANGED names the file
kit_note: the probe imports the kit only for file_provider_domain and the runtime's read_path; the runtime bytes above are the sealed v3.2 ones
